# `check` commands

## `check delete`

Delete this purchase with a required reason and exact expected_version. Cancel its stock and accounting at their original dates; retain immutable history and its number. Requires the explicit family Delete grant and ledger.read, independently of ledger.post. Reconciled, dependent or closed effects refuse atomically.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard; explicit grant required |
| Capability | transaction.check.delete |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.delete` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow check delete 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 1 --operation-key purchase-delete-1 --reason "Remove duplicate purchase" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "check delete", "input": {"check": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "expected_version": 1, "operation_key": "purchase-delete-1"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer | yes | no | — | minimum 1 |
| `operation_key` | `--operation-key` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Permanent retry identity; otherwise the context idempotency key is retained. |
| `check` | `CHECK` | string | yes | no | — | minimum length 1 |

## `check post`

Write a check on a bank account. The bank balance goes down by `amount` and the expense accounts go up by their own line amounts. `account` must be a bank account. `number` is the number written on the face of the cheque; it belongs to this bank account, so two bank accounts can each have a cheque 1001 and a number already used on this one is refused. Leave it out to take the next number from the account’s own next check number, skipping any it has already issued. The journal this posts as keeps its own document reference from the shared series, which is not the check number. `items` accepts purchased items with fractional quantity, unit_cost or amount, description, customer/job, billable and class. Tracked items receive stock once against the bank/card; these are new goods, not payment for an existing bill. `expenses` is zero to 199 lines of account, amount, memo and class saying what the money was spent on; items plus expenses must add up to `amount` exactly, and a total that does not is refused with the difference. A line's own `class_id` is that line's class and a line without one takes the document's `class_id`; set `class_mode` to `none` to leave one line unclassified even when the document carries a class. `pay_to` names who the money went to, from the vendor, customer, employee or other-name lists. When you are unsure which account fits, do not guess: post the line to Uncategorized Expense (Ask My Accountant), or Uncategorized Income for money received, with a memo saying what is unclear. `account uncategorized` lists what is waiting there, and moving an entry to its account later is an ordinary update of the document.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.post` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow check post --account Checking --pay-to-name-type vendor --pay-to-name-id "Northside Supply" --date 2026-04-02 --number 1042 --amount 284.60 --memo "March supplies" --expenses '[{"account":"Office Supplies","amount":"184.60","memo":"Parts"},{"account":"Professional Fees","amount":"100.00","memo":"Filing"}]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Pay Northside Supply" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "check post", "input": {"account": "Checking", "pay_to": {"name_type": "vendor", "name_id": "Northside Supply"}, "date": "2026-04-02", "number": "1042", "amount": "284.60", "memo": "March supplies", "expenses": [{"account": "Office Supplies", "amount": "184.60", "memo": "Parts"}, {"account": "Professional Fees", "amount": "100.00", "memo": "Filing"}]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

Leave it out to take the next number from the account's own next check number, skipping any it has already issued. A number below that pointer is accepted and does not move it backwards; a number already on another cheque drawn on the same account is refused. Leading zeros are kept as typed, and 01001 and 1001 are one number. A number that is not a plain run of digits is a real cheque number with no place in the sequence. |
| `to_be_printed` | `--to-be-printed` | boolean | no | no | false | Print Later: save the check with no number yet and put it in its bank account's print queue; `check print` gives it a number when it is printed. Leave `number` out. |
| `no_number` | `--no-number` | boolean | no | no | false | A payment from the bank account with no cheque behind it: a debit-card purchase, an online bill payment, an automatic withdrawal. It takes no number from the chequebook, never enters the print queue and stays unnumbered when corrected unless a number is typed. The accounting is a check's. Leave `number` and `to_be_printed` out. Do not type a word such as DEBIT as the number: a number is unique on its account, so the second one is refused. |

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|

| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.post`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

## `check print`

Print the queued cheques of one bank account. `first_number` is the number on the first check loaded in the printer (default: the account's next check number); each cheque takes the next number in order, and a number already used on the account is refused rather than skipped. Choose a `style` (voucher, standard, wallet) and, for standard or wallet sheets, `checks_on_first_page` for a partial first sheet. The run and its numbers are recorded and the numbers held until someone answers `check print-confirm`; get the PDF with `check print-pdf`. A cheque dated in a closed period is refused. An agent may prepare a run; confirming it is a person's act.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.print` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow check print --account Checking --first-number 1001 --style voucher --reason "Print this week's checks" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "check print", "input": {"account": "Checking", "first_number": "1001", "style": "voucher"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `account` | `--account` | string | yes | no | — | Bank account ID or canonical full name whose chequebook the cheques are drawn on.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `first_number` | `--first-number` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The number on the first check loaded in the printer; the rest print in order after it. Omit to use the account's next check number. Every number in the run must be free on this account. |
| `style` | `--style` | literal["voucher", "standard", "wallet"] \| null | no | yes | null | Check style; omit for the account's printer setup (voucher by default). |
| `checks` | `--checks` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Print only these queued cheques (transaction IDs), in queue order; omit for every cheque queued on the account. |
| `checks_on_first_page` | `--checks-on-first-page` | integer | no | no | 3 | Standard and wallet checks: how many checks are left on a partial first sheet (1-3; 3 is a full sheet). The partial sheet goes in top edge first.; minimum 1; maximum 3 |

### Command and context options

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.print`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

## `check print-cancel`

Cancel a print run that never reached paper: its cheques go back to the queue and its numbers are released unspoiled. A person's act.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `check print-confirm`

Answer "Did checks print OK?" for a print run. With nothing else, every check printed and carries its number from now on. `failed_from` names the first check that did not print correctly -- it and every later one go back to the queue for a fresh number -- or `failed` lists the ones that did not; their numbers are recorded as spoiled, so `report missing-checks` explains them and they are never handed out again. A person's act: it says what happened to paper in the printer.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.print-confirm` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow check print-confirm 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --failed-from 1003 --reason "Jammed at 1003" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "check print-confirm", "input": {"run": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "failed_from": "1003"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | `RUN` | string | yes | no | — | Print run ID, from `check print`.; minimum length 1; maximum length 64 |
| `failed_from` | `--failed-from` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The number of the first check that did not print correctly; it and every later check in the run go back to the queue for a fresh number, and their numbers are recorded as spoiled. Omit when every check printed. |
| `failed` | `--failed` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | The numbers of the checks that did not print correctly, when they are not one run to the end. |

## `check print-queue`

List the cheques waiting to be printed, by bank account, as the anchor's Select Checks to Print does: checks saved with `to_be_printed` and bill payments by check paid `to_be_printed`, oldest first, with the first check number Print would propose, the printer setup, and any print run still waiting for "Did checks print OK?".

## `check print-setup`

Set a bank account's check printer setup: the default `style` and the fine alignment, in hundredths of an inch (horizontal: positive moves right; vertical: positive moves up). Try offsets first with `check print-alignment`.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |

| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.print-setup` |
| External binary body | none |

### MCP


## `check reprint`

Print one numbered check or bill payment cheque again. Without `new_number` it prints with the number it has and nothing about it changes. With `new_number` it prints on a new check: the old number is recorded as spoiled and the cheque carries the new one (refused for a cheque dated in a closed period). Get the PDF with `check print-pdf --run`. A person's act.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.reprint` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow check reprint 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --new-number 1010 --reason "Coffee on check 1004" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "check reprint", "input": {"check": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "new_number": "1010"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `check` | `CHECK` | string | yes | no | — | The printed cheque: its transaction ID.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `new_number` | `--new-number` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Print it on a new check with this number; the number it carried is recorded as spoiled. Omit to reprint it with the number it has. |
| `style` | `--style` | literal["voucher", "standard", "wallet"] \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `checks_on_first_page` | `--checks-on-first-page` | integer | no | no | 3 | minimum 1; maximum 3 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | Version of the cheque document, when the reprint must not race a correction. |

## `check show`

Show a check: its current or a selected earlier revision, the bank account it is drawn on, who it was paid to, the expense lines, the posting batches and the figures on its own footer, including the check number that revision was written with. A check is named by its id or by its check number; when two bank accounts both issued that number, both are named and neither is opened.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | ledger.read |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.show` |
| External binary body | none |

## `check update`

Correct a check, including moving it to another bank account or giving it a different number. A cheque that moves keeps its number unless a new one is supplied; the number it had stays on the revision that carried it and is never handed out automatically again. Every field is optional and a field left out keeps what was captured. Supply `expenses` to replace the whole grid, carrying each surviving row’s `line_id` and omitting it on a new row. The same replacement rule applies independently to `items`; an omitted grid retains its captured facts. Leave `expenses` out to correct the header alone and keep the rows exactly as they were captured. A replaced grid resolves `class_mode: inherit` against the `class_id` supplied on this call, so send the document’s class again with the rows if it still applies. The old accounting is reversed at its original date and replaced in full at the new one; every earlier revision stays readable.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow check update 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 1 --amount 300.00 --expenses '[{"account":"Office Supplies","amount":"200.00","memo":"Parts"},{"account":"Professional Fees","amount":"100.00","memo":"Filing"}]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Parts line was understated" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "check update", "input": {"check": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "expected_version": 1, "amount": "300.00", "expenses": [{"account": "Office Supplies", "amount": "200.00", "memo": "Parts"}, {"account": "Professional Fees", "amount": "100.00", "memo": "Filing"}]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--clear FIELD` | Set a nullable field to null; repeatable. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.update`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

## `check void`

Void a check with a required reason: the cheque that was lost, stale or never cashed. Its accounting is reversed exactly, at the check’s own date, so no earlier period moves; its number stays occupied and its history stays readable.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.void` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow check void 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 2 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Never cashed" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "check void", "input": {"check": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV", "expected_version": 2}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `check` | `CHECK` | string | yes | no | — | minimum length 1 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer \| null | no | yes | null | — |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/check.void`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
| `Idempotency-Key` | optional | Retry-safe key for this create command |

| `E_PERIOD_CLOSED` | An affected accounting date is in a closed period. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
